newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gold to consolidate but only short term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gold to consolidate but only short term.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold was forecast to consolidate after its falls of the past two days, technical analysts said.
Although it was likely to stay in a tight range Tuesday, the drift to the downside would prevail.
GOLD -
Consolidation was forecast for a gold market still shaken after falls to 12-year lows in only two trading days.
"We would expect to see some initial consolidation between $314.50 and $323-$326 but that would cap it," said technical analyst Fran Skelley at Credit Suisse First Boston.
However, the downside trend would continue with targets at $309.80, $303.00 and the 1985 low of $284.50 to be probed within a three month period, Skelley said.
"These markets have been going sideways for so long that now a trend has begun it will be very significant," she said.
Dealers noted that gold was heavily oversold with an RSI of 16 but this was making little difference to the market's posture with all sides trying to be short.
At 0810 GMT gold was indicated at $317.60/$318.10, down from Monday's London close of $318.30/$318.80.
SILVER -
Some of the bearish attention has switched to silver in the past 24 hours witnessed by its gap fall to $4.25/$4.27 on Tuesday morning.
"The $4.34 was a significant support level and also an uptrend," one analyst said while Credit Suisse First Boston's Skelley suggested the target for silver was now the 1991/92 lows.
"I would expect to see consolidation short-term but the $4.36-$4.43 will cap the upside while there will be psychological support at $4.02 and $4.00," she said.
Under $4.00 there could be buying interest at $3.91 and $3.78.
At 0810 GMT silver was indicted at $4.25/$4.27 down 19 cents from Monday's London close.
PLATINUM -
Light selling ahead of the forecast start of Russian 1997 exports later this week was pushing platinum lower, analysts said.
The downside had accelerated after the breakthrough of the $415-$418 level which marked a retracement from the early June high of $505.00.
The market might have to rely on physical tightness and psychology to hold above $400.00 this week, dealers and analysts said.
At 0810 GMT platinum was indicated at $406.00/$409.00. down about $4.50 from London's Monday close.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
